author: Unreal Engine
description:
A quick recap of the full Getting Started with Unreal MCP course, from terminology and setup to troubleshooting, toolsets, the Terminal plugin workflow, configuration, tips, and FAQs. Now you're ready to turn AI into action in your own projects. Thanks for watching!

#UnrealEngine #UE5 #UnrealMCP #GameDev
title: Unreal MCP Recap: Everything You Need to Get Started

author: Unreal Engine
description:
Spend less time waiting and more time iterating with five tips we picked up while building this course. Turn off background CPU throttling (in our testing, a 46-second MCP call dropped to about one second), plan before you build, consider C++ over Blueprints for complex logic, use a continuous improvement loop with your agent.md file, and enable only the toolsets you need when working with small context models.

#UnrealEngine #UE5 #UnrealMCP #Blueprints
title: 5 Unreal MCP Tips: Cut Tool Calls from 46 Seconds to 1

author: Unreal Engine
description:
Unreal MCP is the official, Epic-supported way to connect your favorite agentic AI tools directly to Unreal Engine. Built on the open MCP standard, it lets AI agents understand your project and take action in the editor: creating, modifying, testing, and iterating on your work. In this course, Senior Unreal Engine Instructor Sam Deiter walks you through everything you need to get started with Unreal MCP (Experimental in Unreal Engine 5.8): key terminology, the seven-step setup, troubleshooting and debugging, toolsets, the in-editor Terminal plugin workflow, configuration settings, time-saving tips, and answers to the most common questions.

#UnrealEngine #UE5 #UnrealMCP #GameDev
title: Getting Started with Unreal MCP | Turn AI into Action in UE 5.8

author: Unreal Engine
description:
Find out exactly where a tool call is failing. This lesson shows you how to follow MCP activity in the Output Log, then set up the MCP Inspector, the official debugging client for the open MCP standard, to list and call tools directly with no AI agent in the loop. If a call fails there, the issue is the tool or the server, not your prompt.

#UnrealEngine #UE5 #UnrealMCP #Debugging
title: How to Debug Unreal MCP with the Output Log & MCP Inspector

author: Unreal Engine
description:
Connect the agentic AI tools that work for you, including Claude Code, Cursor, Visual Studio Code, Gemini CLI, and Codex, to Unreal Engine in seven steps. This lesson covers creating your project, enabling the Unreal MCP and All Toolsets plugins, turning on Auto Start Server, generating your client config, starting the server, launching your harness from the project root, and testing it with your first prompts, from checking your selected actors to placing a ring of 12 lit cubes.

#UnrealEngine #UE5 #UnrealMCP
title: How to Set Up Unreal MCP in UE 5.8 | Connect Claude Code, Cursor & More

author: Unreal Engine
description:
Before setting up Unreal MCP, get to know the six terms you'll hear throughout this course: MCP, model, harness, context, agent.md, and toolset. Learn what each one means, how they fit together, and how Unreal MCP lets you build with the AI tools that work for you, so you can swap models like Claude or Codex without changing anything else in your project.

#UnrealEngine #UE5 #UnrealMCP #ModelContextProtocol
title: Unreal MCP Explained: MCP, Models, Harnesses, Context & Toolsets

author: Unreal Engine
description:
Answers to the questions everyone asks about Unreal MCP: why it won't connect, which engine versions are supported, the official Epic-supported plugin vs. community servers, using local models, security and what data leaves your machine, what AI agents can and can't do in your project, writing your own tools, team use and source control, undo, and whether it's ready for production.

#UnrealEngine #UE5 #UnrealMCP
title: Unreal MCP FAQ: Is It Safe? Local Models, Engine Versions & More

author: Unreal Engine
description:
If your AI agent can see Unreal MCP but can't take action in your project, there are three things to check: where you launched your agent from, whether the server is running, and whether any toolsets are enabled. You'll also learn why the editor can appear to freeze during long tool calls, and how breaking big jobs into smaller requests keeps your iteration moving.

#UnrealEngine #UE5 #UnrealMCP #Troubleshooting
title: Unreal MCP Not Connecting? How to Fix "Agent Sees No Tools"

author: Unreal Engine
description:
A quick reference for where Unreal MCP's settings live. Revisit the Model Context Protocol section of Editor Preferences, including Auto Start Server and Enable Tool Search, browse the ModelContextProtocol console commands, and learn why every tool in this course is editor-only.

#UnrealEngine #UE5 #UnrealMCP #GameDev
title: Unreal MCP Settings & Console Commands You Should Know

author: Unreal Engine
description:
Keep your AI agent and your project in one workflow. Learn how to enable the Terminal plugin, point the in-editor terminal at the folder holding your .mcp.json file, and launch your agent right inside Unreal Engine, plus a quick fix if your terminal text looks wrong.

#UnrealEngine #UE5 #UnrealMCP
title: Unreal MCP Terminal Plugin: Use Your AI Agent Without Leaving Unreal

author: Unreal Engine
description:
Every action an AI agent takes in your project starts as a toolset. Learn how toolsets and the tool registry work together, why Tool Search shows your agent just three discovery tools instead of hundreds, when to run ModelContextProtocol.RefreshTools, and where to start if you want to build your own toolsets in Python or C++ around how you create.
